answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. What makes it robust is that honest graders are financially motivated to reject the cluster, so fake votes lose their value before verdicts are tallied. Consider a forge as the anchor of the cost. A quartz stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a reef holds...
